The '''Players Committee&ndash;Lucasfilm agreement''' is the community name for the arrangement that lets the volunteer [[Players Committee]] (PC) support ''Star Wars'' CCG. Under it the PC continued organized play and free electronic Virtual cards after Decipher lost the commercial Lucasfilm license. The PC works with the cooperation of '''Decipher and Lucasfilm Ltd.''' under explicit distribution restrictions; the full legal contract has not been published.<ref name="pc1">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611042314/http://decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee1.html The Star Wars Players' Committee], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002)</ref><ref name="pcabout">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/about-us/ About Us], starwarsccg.org</ref><ref name="pcabout2">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/about/ About], starwarsccg.org</ref><ref name="pcabout3">[https://playerscommittee.org/about/ About], playerscommittee.org</ref>

== After Decipher lost the license ==

Main article: [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]].

In '''December 2001''', Decipher announced it had been unable to extend its Lucasfilm license to continue producing the game.<ref name="pcabout" /> Unable to keep producing, marketing, or supporting the commercial product, Decipher formed a volunteer '''Players' Committee''' / Player Advocate structure so fans could continue tournaments, rulings, and support.<ref name="pc1" /><ref name="pcabout" /> Decipher announced the first Player Advocates on '''25 January 2002'''.<ref name="pc1" />

=== Stated restrictions (PC About) ===

The PC may create new cards '''with restrictions''', including:<ref name="pcabout" />

* Cards could only be distributed '''electronically'''
* The PC could '''not''' create physical cards
* The PC could '''not''' utilize '''new images''' from the ''Star Wars'' films
* Everything the PC created must be distributed '''for free''' (no sale of PC-created cards)

With the cooperation of Decipher and Lucasfilm Ltd., the PC began releasing Virtual cards in '''2002'''.<ref name="pcabout" /><ref name="tfn2002">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.Net, 12 February 2002</ref> They were printable game-text overlays, and later fuller frames, placed over existing Decipher cards (see [[V-slips]] and [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]).<ref name="pcabout" />

PC forum discussions of tournament proxy policy and related limits also refer to the PC's agreements with Lucasfilm and Decipher.<ref name="proxyforum">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?p=1372122 Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums] &mdash; proxy / agreement discussion (forum post)</ref>

== Disney takeover of Lucasfilm (context) ==

The Walt Disney Company announced its agreement to acquire Lucasfilm on '''30 October 2012'''.<ref name="disney2012">[https://thewaltdisneycompany.com/news/disney-acquire-lucasfilm/ Disney to Acquire Lucasfilm], The Walt Disney Company, 30 October 2012</ref><ref name="disney8k">[https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1001039/000119312512441509/d429302d8k.htm Walt Disney Company Form 8-K], 30 October 2012</ref>

The PC About page still describes the PC's work as done '''with the cooperation of Decipher and Lucasfilm Ltd.''' and publishes no separate Disney-era agreement.<ref name="pcabout" />

=== Later contact with Lucasfilm ===

A May 2018 ''The Ringer'' feature interviewed PC lead advocate Scott Lingrell and others. According to the article, about eight years earlier the PC wrote to Lucasfilm about reclaiming a commercial license, and Lucasfilm declined manufacturing.<ref name="ringer2018">[https://www.theringer.com/2018/5/21/17374528/star-wars-customizable-card-game-player-community The Force Is Strong With This 'Star Wars' Subculture], Ben Lindbergh, ''The Ringer'', 21 May 2018</ref> Community representatives later met Lucasfilm staff, who said the volunteer work was welcome; the PC has remained careful not to lose that trust.<ref name="ringer2018" />

Separate commercial ''Star Wars'' tabletop licenses, such as Fantasy Flight Games' 2011 Lucasfilm games license, are a different arrangement from PC Virtual support for Decipher's out-of-print CCG.<ref name="icv2ffg">[https://icv2.com/articles/games/view/20728/ffg-acquires-star-wars-games-license FFG Acquires 'Star Wars' Games License], ICv2, 2 August 2011</ref>

== Continuity of Virtual program ==

The PC continued releasing free Virtual slips and sets after 2012, including the '''2014 Virtual Card Reset''' and ongoing Current Virtual sets (see [[History of the Players Committee]] and [[Formats]]).
